result.summary: Introduces BlockTemplateManager to manage block creation, tip tracking, and submission state, while using mempool diagram notifications to incrementally track fee inflow for waitNext instead of rebuilding full templates every polling tick. It also updates template consumers across RPC and testing to avoid unnecessary full-block copies.
result.problem: Currently, waitNext repeatedly locks cs_main and assembles a full block template on every tick merely to detect if mempool fee inflow warrants an updated template. In addition, mining free functions scattered in miner.cpp require threading ChainstateManager and KernelNotifications redundantly.

categories.evidence: Refactors block template generation, waitNext fee staleness tracking, and introduces BlockTemplateManager in src/node/miner.cpp.
categories.rationale: P2 because replacing full block assembly on every waitNext poll with incremental chunk-fee tracking removes unnecessary cs_main lock contention and CPU load during block generation for mining pools. It delivers meaningful operational benefits to Stratum v2 and mining template consumers.

categories.rationale: P3 because caching fee rate diagram chunks in ChangeSet and emitting MempoolUpdated provides a clean event hook for subsystems tracking fee rate updates without holding the mempool lock, but does not alter mempool acceptance policy or data structures.

result.card: PR 35581 introduces a BlockTemplateManager and implements incremental fee-inflow tracking for waitNext, eliminating the need to lock cs_main and construct complete block templates on every polling tick. This provides significant CPU and lock contention relief for mining operations and template providers. Review is currently best focused on base PR 35675, which extracts the BlockTemplateManager groundwork at reviewer request. Concept support is strong, with fuzz tests already having identified an upstream mining bug (#35580).
